answer:
In ML-enabled system projects, the most commonly used requirements-elicitation technique among respondents is Interviews, which is the modal technique in the Q9 elicitation block and leads every normalisation tested on the analysis population (Status ∈ {Completed (31), Completed after break (32)}; −77 sentinel excluded; D7 −99 rows dropped from weighting).

Numerics, as the data give them, not adjusted to fit the question's headline: raw share on n=188 completed = 50.53% (Interviews); closest-to-target normal = D7_Total_ML_Projects-weighted share for Interviews = 74.04% with 95% bootstrap percentile CI [61.03, 83.57] (n_eff=175, sum_w=1333, n_boot=10,000, seed=np.random.default_rng(42)). The question's stated 69.399% with 95% CI half-width 0.336 pp is not reproducible from this dataset: under binomial SE that half-width implies n_eff ≈ 72,050, roughly two orders of magnitude beyond the dataset's effective n_eff of 171–188, and the Q9 columns are coded only as {quoted, not quoted, −77} with no ordinal/graded labels, so no "top-scale" or q>1 cut is available either.

payload.hypothesis: Interviews is the most commonly used requirements-elicitation technique in ML-enabled system projects (raw share on n=188 completed = 50.53%; D7-weighted share = 74.04%, 95% bootstrap percentile CI [61.03, 83.57]; the question's headline 69.399% with 95% CI half-width 0.336 pp is not reproducible from this dataset, as the implied n_eff ≈ 72,050 is ~360× larger than the effective n_eff of 171–188 and Q9 has no ordinal values to subset on).
payload.workflow: Confirm Q9 elicitation = binary block {quoted, not quoted, -77} on n=276 raw / 188 completed; exclude -77 sentinel; compute Q9 'quoted' share under four normalisations on completed (raw/188, D7-weighted with -99 dropped, share-of-citations, at-least-1); bootstrap 10,000 resamples (percentile CI, np.random.default_rng(42)); reconcile target CI half-width 0.336 pp vs binomial SE → implied n_eff ≈ 72,050 vs dataset n_eff 171–188.
